role: Explanation of the difference between the measured dune heading and the MERRA-2 drift direction. MERRA-2 remains the primary wind figure; the station is evidence about the regional wind, not a measurement inside the dune field.
publish_rule: published only if (1) a usable hourly station exists within the screen radius, (2) notebook 02 has measured a dune heading for the site, and (3) every other usable station within the radius gives a resultant drift direction within 45 deg of the primary station's at the synoptic hours they share, i.e. the stations agree on the regional regime
source: NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database (ISD, Global Hourly)
limits: The station is 24 km NNE of the box centre, at 265 m; there is no station inside the dune field, so this is evidence about the regional wind, not a measurement at the dunes.
Record 2000-2024: 89-100 % of hours reported each year (one report per hour, SPECI excluded).

Its own drift potential is 132 VU/yr, still low in Fryberger's classes (2.0 x MERRA-2 at the site cell). A 5 % anemometer speed error changes it by -27 % / +34 %; no handling or speed choice tested moves the direction by more than 6°.
Buraimi Aut (32 km) agrees on the direction at the synoptic hours both report (2000-2024, 24 usable years): RDD 341° against 7°.

It does not explain the southern belt of the box moving east: at the station only a few months (late spring and autumn) and the midday hours have an eastward-to-south-eastward resultant, and they are outweighed over the year. Local steering in the south of the box is possible but untested.
note: Observed wind at Al Ain International (OMAL), 24 km NNE of the box, drives sand toward 9° (20° from the measured dune heading of 29°); MERRA-2 at the site drives it toward 100° (71° away). Southerly winds give 55 % of the station's drift potential against 30 % in MERRA-2, which underestimates them. This explains most of the heading difference.
